summary: CCC-built 1938 two-story log lookout on Huckleberry Mountain in the Bridger-Teton; manned until 1957, still standing, current access unconfirmed.

facts.design: L-4 cab with catwalk on a log crib base
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Bridger-Teton National Forest

events.note: Built by the CCC to a standard USFS design; the register and nomination both give 1938
First manned in 1939, per the nomination
Sheffield Creek fire; forest lookout Dave Adams forced to leave the structure
A 1942 newspaper item calls Huckleberry one of the permanent stations built that year; this conflicts with the 1938 build date and is unresolved
Named in a July 1954 item as a position to be manned within the next week
Abandoned for regular lookout service after the 1957 season
Added to the National Register on July 8, 1983
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on August 9, 2011
Crews wrapped the lookout in protective material in case the Berry Fire reached its ridge

corrections.why: The nomination and firelookout.com both give 9,615 feet (about 2,930 m); the register's 7,209 feet (2,197 m) is the only lower figure. Needs a human check against a survey or USGS source.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination gives the structure as 20 feet high, which matches the record's 6.1 m. The register gives no height. Cab width is still disputed: 14 feet in the register, 15 by 17 feet in the nomination.

sources.title: Huckleberry Lookout, National Register of Historic Places nomination form (No. 83003365)

notes_for_editor: Build year 1938 is supported by three sources, but a 1942 newspaper item (quoted on westlookouts) calls Huckleberry a permanent station that year; not resolved. Current status is unconfirmed: the newest dated text read is the register entry (2011 registration; 'slated for restoration') and firelookout.com 'Standing'. Elevation conflict (7,209 ft register vs 9,615 ft nomination and firelookout) is proposed as a correction for human review. Page budget was used up before reading the Wyoming SHPO page, the Jackson Hole Mountain Resort page or the Hiking Project page; search snippets claim restoration and overnight use, but those were not read or cited, so check them before any access statement is changed. No new photos.
